transcript:
Header: 2026-03-20 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE); Maya Singh (Redwood SE); Jordan Lee (NexaHealth CTO); Priya Patel (Platform Eng); Carlos Rivera (Data Scientist)

Summary: quick sync on onboarding steps, access status, initial perf runs and next steps

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, um thanks for joining, we're at the usual time — alex here from Redwood, maya's with me from SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Jordan Lee: Good thanks, busy week but ready to go
[00:12] Maya Singh: Hi all, i'll take the tech bits today, want to get through access, bench results, and any blockers
[00:20] Priya Patel: Sounds good

[02:15] Alex Chen: Quick status — can you confirm if the VPC peering request was routed to your infra team? I see a note from Priya that they started the ticket
[02:25] Priya Patel: Yeah we opened ticket TKT-1123, infra replied but they had a question about route tables. I'm happy to walk through with maya after this call, the peering window we can do next tuesday the 24th
[02:40] Maya Singh: Ok great, for the peering we need 3 things: a BGP or static routes, the subnets we published, and port rules 1024-65535 for our health checks. Also, if you're doing private deployment we'll need the KMS info for key wrapping
[03:05] Jordan Lee: On KMS we use HashiCorp Vault but we can expose an HSM-backed key — needs approval from security

[05:00] Maya Singh: On the access side we got the test account creds for the staging cluster, Carlos confirmed the API keys work. We started a small perf run, baseline was run on hosted endpoint (redwood-hosted) with 2K requests, avg p50 latency 180ms, p95 420ms — but that was with our default batching settings
[05:30] Carlos Rivera: Note: the transcript might say 180ms but i think p50 was closer to 220ms, the auto-transcription swapped some numbers earlier in our local notes
[06:10] Maya Singh: Right; when we re-ran with dedicated-sized batcher and kv-cache warm flag enabled latency improved to p50 140ms, p95 360ms. We also tested a quantized variant which dropped token cost but added ~20ms latency in generation step
[07:00] Jordan Lee: That matches our expectation — cost vs latency tradeoffs. We care mostly about 95th percentile under load because our UI is sensitive

[09:00] Alex Chen: Great — couple of items on security: Jordan, are you tracking SOC2 and any data residency reqs?
[09:12] Jordan Lee: SOC2 is a must. Also we have EU data residency concerns for EU customers, though primary pilot data is US-based. We need audit logs, retention controls and to know who sees the logs
[09:35] Maya Singh: Redwood can enable audit logs and we support per-route retention in the console. For private deployments we can offer customer-managed retention and KMS integration. I'll attach the SOC2 + security pack to the AE follow up

[12:00] Carlos Rivera: One weird thing we saw — cold-start kv cache caused a few 2s outliers, looks like model cache warm wasn't preloaded for some prefixes
[12:20] Maya Singh: Yeah cold KV cache warmup is common — options: prefix caching for hot prompts, or pre-warm by replaying a small set of representative prompts during off-peak. We can script that as part of onboarding
[12:55] Priya Patel: If we pre-warm, does that count against our usage? We want to avoid unexpected billed tokens
[13:10] Maya Singh: Good question — pre-warm runs are billed as normal tokens, but we can keep the sample small, usually a few hundred prompts is enough for warmup

[15:30] Alex Chen: On pricing — we'll send an updated SOW that includes Dedicated reserved hours and a burst policy. Jordan, did you have a target for monthly committed spend?
[15:44] Jordan Lee: We're aiming to keep pilot under $8k per month, but for production we expect to allocate more if latency SLOs are met
[16:05] Alex Chen: Ok we'll model costs for both hosted and dedicated — show the per-token math and the dedicated committed discount. I'll include Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching and quantization to reach your cost target

[18:00] Maya Singh: Technical note — during our stress test we saw tail latency increase when concurrency > 40, likely due to batching head-of-line. We recommended setting concurrency throttle at the route level for demo traffic
[18:25] Carlos Rivera: Also saw model-variant fallback trigger once capacity hit, so we need to ensure routing policy won't silently switch to lower-quality variants without alerting
[18:50] Maya Singh: We'll configure explicit alerting for model fallback and also a tag in traces

[21:00] Priya Patel: On SSO — we tried to upload SAML metadata but the staging portal threw an error 'invalid entity id' — Jordan will get metadata from Okta
[21:20] Jordan Lee: I'll send the metadata post-call, expect it by Wednesday

[24:00] Alex Chen: Action items recap — maya to run 5k latency benchmark with realistic prompt set, capture p50/p95 and token cost, due next friday the 27th. Alex to send pricing and SOW by Weds the 25th. Jordan to provide SSO metadata and KMS decision by Mon the 23rd. Priya to confirm peering window Tues the 24th and validate firewall rules
[24:45] Priya Patel: Also we'll coordinate maintenance windows for pre-warm scripts

[27:30] Jordan Lee: One more blocker — procurement wants to see subprocessor list and DPAs before we sign pilot paperwork
[27:40] Alex Chen: Will include subprocessor and DPA in follow up, we have standard legal pack. Also we can provide a short privacy note for bench data

[30:00] Maya Singh: I'll also include steps to enable audit logs and per-route retention in the runbook. We can demo the console retention toggle in next call

[33:00] Carlos Rivera: Quick question on metrics — do you surface per-route token breakdown? We want to map cost to feature
[33:10] Maya Singh: Yes, console shows token-level breakdown by route and model, with cost attribution. We'll share a sample dashboard screenshot

[36:00] Alex Chen: Ok i think that's everything. Any other concerns?
[36:10] Jordan Lee: No, just timeline — we want to be ready to expand pilot scale mid-april if benchmarks look good
[36:25] Alex Chen: Great. We'll reconvene next week same time. I'll send calendar invite. Thanks everyone

[38:00] End of recording

Notes: transcription imperfect in a few numeric places; refer to attached benchmark spreadsheet and security pack (links shared in chat).
